evals.prompt: Fresh Vite + React app. I installed @viraui/react but everything looks unstyled and toasts don't show. Give me the root bootstrap steps.
evals.expected_output: Ask default foundation vs App Studio custom theme before installing @viraui/foundation/fonts. Then ordered bootstrap: peers, one theme CSS before components, fonts, preflight after theme, JS side-effect imports in app root (not CSS @import), canonical Dialog/Tooltip/Toast providers in root layout, authority from @viraui/react/specs/foundation/bootstrap.xml (hub checklist). End with a Markdown setup-recap table (status + what landed), not prose-only.
assertions: Asks (or requires an answer for) default Vira/@viraui/foundation theme vs App Studio custom CSS before installing foundation/fonts
Lists JavaScript side-effect imports in app root — not CSS @import for bootstrap
Theme CSS loads before Vira components render
Mentions Toast.Provider with viewport at app root
References @viraui/react/specs/foundation/bootstrap.xml (or hub setup checklist) for authoritative order
May use bootstrap.md playbook; authority remains foundation/bootstrap.xml
Does not invent component APIs or skip overlay providers
Ends with a Markdown setup-recap table (or equivalent visual status grid) of steps done / skipped / blocked — not prose-only

evals.prompt: Next.js App Router project — where do I put theme, preflight, and Dialog.Provider?
evals.expected_output: Framework-specific entry guidance from frameworks.md: root layout module, import order, overlay providers wrapping children. Theme line depends on prior default vs Studio choice.
assertions: Names root layout or app entry as import site
Keeps bootstrap imports as JS imports in that module
Includes Dialog.Provider (and related overlay providers) at root
Points to frameworks.md or foundation/bootstrap.xml rather than guessing paths

evals.prompt: Can I @import @viraui/react/preflight.css inside my global.css to keep things tidy?
evals.expected_output: No — bootstrap must be JS side-effect imports in app root per setup skill; explain why and give correct pattern.
assertions: Rejects CSS @import for Vira bootstrap chain
Prescribes JS side-effect import in app root entry
Does not suggest per-page provider patches as the primary fix

evals.prompt: How do I install the ViraUI agent skills into my coding agent?
evals.expected_output: npx skills add vira-soft/viraui-skills; no npm @viraui/skills; no private monorepo clone.
assertions: Gives npx skills add vira-soft/viraui-skills (or equivalent GitHub owner/repo)
Does not prescribe npm view @viraui/skills dist.tarball or a registry .tgz URL
Does not prescribe npx @viraui/skills or a wipe-copy package installer
Does not tell the consumer to clone the private monorepo

evals.prompt: Fresh Vite app with @viraui/react. I already use lucide-react. Should I also install @viraui/icons before first render?
evals.expected_output: @viraui/icons is optional — install only to use Vira named glyphs from @viraui/icons/react. Icon slots accept any ReactNode: lucide-react, other icon libraries, or custom SVG. Chrome defaults ship inlined in @viraui/react. Do not add @viraui/icons as a required peer.
assertions: States @viraui/icons is optional, not a required bootstrap peer
Allows lucide-react or another icon library in Vira icon slots
Does not require installing @viraui/icons when the app already has an icon library
Does not say content icons must come from @viraui/icons/react

evals.prompt: Custom theme: what do --radius-* and --corner-shape mean for pill shapes?
evals.expected_output: Radius scale + corner-shape; with --effect-corner-shape on, theme corner-shape can cap full/pill radius. Consumer raw CSS: set corner-shape: unset locally. ViraUI components set internal --__corner-shape for token full / pills — no consumer data-radius.
assertions: Mentions corner-shape interaction with full / pill radius
Says consumer local override is corner-shape: unset (or equivalent) for raw CSS
Does not invent data-radius or public --__corner-shape consumer API

evals.prompt: Bootstrap my app with ViraUI. Install whatever theme packages you need.
evals.expected_output: Stop and ask: default @viraui/foundation theme (plus matching fontsource) OR App Studio custom theme.css. Do not install @viraui/foundation or fonts until the consumer answers. If any steps already ran, end with a setup-recap table marking theme choice as blocked.
assertions: Asks default foundation theme vs App Studio / custom generated CSS before installing @viraui/foundation
Does not install @viraui/foundation in the same turn without a theme-choice answer
Does not install @fontsource-variable packages before theme choice is known
When work stops mid-checklist, includes a setup-recap table with theme choice (or later steps) marked blocked / pending

evals.prompt: I'll use my App Studio export. Here is theme.css with @font-face src urls to cdn.jsdelivr.net/fontsource/fonts/raleway:vf@… and --font-family-body: Geist Variable. Wire it up.
evals.expected_output: Skip @viraui/foundation. Save/import the pasted CSS as the theme sheet. Detect fontsource ids (raleway from URL; geist from --font-family-*). Install @fontsource-variable/raleway and @fontsource-variable/geist, import their wght.css after theme CSS, strip or ignore CDN @font-face quick-setup blocks, then preflight. Close with a Markdown setup-recap table of what landed.
assertions: Does not install @viraui/foundation for the Studio custom path
Imports the consumer-saved Studio CSS as the theme sheet
Installs or imports @fontsource-variable packages derived from the CSS (raleway and geist)
Keeps import order theme → fonts → preflight via JS side-effect imports
Ends with a Markdown setup-recap table showing Studio theme path, fonts, and preflight status

evals.prompt: Wire ViraUI into this Vite app. package.json has tailwindcss and the CSS entry is `@import "tailwindcss";`. Keep Tailwind utilities.
evals.expected_output: Warn that Tailwind (and other CSS frameworks) ship a preflight/reset that can fight @viraui/react/preflight.css and break ViraUI. Ask what to do. Recommend keeping Vira preflight and NOT importing Tailwind preflight — replace full `@import "tailwindcss"` with theme + utilities only (`@import "tailwindcss/theme.css" layer(theme);` and `@import "tailwindcss/utilities.css" layer(utilities);`). Do not silently keep the full Tailwind bundle. End with setup-recap noting CSS-framework coexistence.
assertions: Warns that Tailwind preflight/reset (or equivalent) can conflict with ViraUI preflight
Asks the consumer what to do rather than silently keeping `@import "tailwindcss"`
Recommends omitting Tailwind preflight and shows theme.css + utilities.css layered imports (or equivalent no-preflight pattern)
Does not tell the consumer to drop @viraui/react/preflight.css in favor of Tailwind preflight
Mentions the same class of risk for other framework resets (e.g. Bootstrap reboot) when relevant
Ends with a setup-recap table that records CSS-framework coexistence / warning status

evals.prompt: Next.js app already has Bootstrap CSS (reboot). Adding @viraui/react — anything I should change?
evals.expected_output: Warn that Bootstrap reboot/reset CSS can override or fight ViraUI preflight baselines. Ask whether to keep Bootstrap reset, drop it, or scope it. Prefer keeping @viraui/react/preflight.css and removing or isolating Bootstrap's global reset/reboot when coexisting.
assertions: Warns about Bootstrap reboot/reset vs ViraUI preflight conflict
Asks how to handle the third-party reset rather than ignoring it
Keeps @viraui/react/preflight.css as the Vira baseline
Does not claim Bootstrap and Vira preflight are always safe together with no changes

evals.prompt: I want Text and Title sizes fixed at their largest step — no fluid scaling when the viewport shrinks. How do I turn that off?
evals.expected_output: Set --effect-fluid-typography: initial on the theme root (:root or html). Empty/unset keeps fluid clamp on (brand default). Off locks Text/Title to each size’s theme scale token (--font-scale-body-* / --font-scale-display / --font-scale-h*). No React prop or data-* on Text/Title. Text size s and xs stay fixed either way.
assertions: Names --effect-fluid-typography: initial as the opt-out
Says off locks Text/Title at theme scale tokens (or equivalent fixed-at-token wording)
Does not invent a fluid/static React prop or data-* on Text/Title
Mentions empty/unset (or brand default) keeps fluid on
